To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the experimental thermal and flow condensation characteristics of refrigerants in pipe minichannel are strongly dependent on the refrigerant composition.

the experimental results of homogeneous refrigerants and zeotropic solutions condensation in pipe channels are comparable and that the developed correlations are compatible with the experimental results within ±25% in all tested refrigerants.
the condensation of R134a, R404A, 407C and 410A in pipe minichannel is a complex process and the existing correlations are not accurate enough.
In summary, our research is concerned with
condensation in pipe microchannels, which are used in the refrigeration systems.
the development of a method for the calculation of refrigerant condensation heat transfer in minichannels.
a comprehensive study of refrigerant condensation and the development of correlations for the calculation of heat transfer and frictional pressure losses in pipe minichannel heat exchangers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no correlations available in the literature for condensation in pipe mini-channels which are sufficiently accurate for practical use.
the condensation of refrigerants and zeotropic solutions in pipe minichannel flow is a complex phenomenon and requires further research.
the condensation process of zeotropic solutions is much more complicated than for pure refrigerants and requires further research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of the experimental tests of the condensation of R404A, 407C and 410A in minichannels are not sufficiently known and require further studies.
the condensation process is more complex than it is usually assumed in the literature.

there are significant differences in the results of the tests of homogeneous refrigerant and zeotropic solutions condensation in pipe microchannels and the calculated results of the correlations of other authors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lack of reliable correlations for refrigerant condensation.
there is still a need to develop a more accurate model of condensation in minichannels.
condensation in minichannels of small diameters is characterized by a significant increase in heat transfer compared to condensation in channels of large diameters.
